narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Navigator's Chart"**

The site is a calm chart table with one lit instrument on it. Pages are cool paper with deep navy ink, ruled with fine survey lines. The one loud object is the navy instrument panel in the hero, where Compass takes a reading of a change and shows it in Needle Cyan. Everything else stays quiet so the reading carries the page.

Density is moderate and generous with space. Sections alternate between plain paper, a faint paper tint and full navy bands. Type is a confident grotesque with tight negative tracking for headings, and a monospace for anything a person would type or a tool would print. Components are tactile and confident: solid pills, clear selected states and meters that fill tick by tick.

The site has light and dark themes and follows the visitor's system setting. In dark mode the paper becomes navy, but the instrument stays a navy panel in both themes. The light paper theme is the reference design.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper and deep navy ink, with one navy instrument as the focal object.
Needle Cyan marks a reading or a selection, and almost nothing else.
Flat and tonal everywhere, with a single lifted object.
Grotesque headings with tight negative tracking; monospace for commands, paths and stage names.
Pill-shaped controls and softly rounded panels.

rules.name: The One Needle Rule
rules.body: Needle Cyan marks a reading or a selection. Do not use it for decoration, large fills or body text on paper.

rules.name: The Navy Instrument Rule
rules.body: The instrument is navy in both themes. Do not invert it to a light panel in light mode or a cyan panel in dark mode.

rules.name: The Status Is Colour Plus Words Rule
rules.body: Every status badge carries its word ("Planned", "Shipped"), and Shelved is also struck through. Colour never carries the status alone.

rules.name: The Typed Text Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything a visitor would type, copy or see printed by Compass uses IBM Plex Mono. Prose about it does not.

rules.name: The Tight Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings use negative tracking that grows with size (`-0.01em` for titles up to `-0.03em` for display) and balanced wrapping.

rules.name: The One Lifted Object Rule
rules.body: Only the instrument casts a shadow. Cards, buttons, code rows and news items stay flat at rest and on hover. They show state with border, tone or underline changes instead.

dos: keep Needle Cyan for readings and selections on navy, as the One Needle Rule says.
keep the instrument navy in both themes, and keep it the only object with a shadow.
use IBM Plex Mono for commands, paths, prompts and stage names.
pair every status colour with its word, and strike through Shelved.
show hover and focus with border, tone and underline changes, and always keep the 3px focus ring: navy on paper, Sky Signal on navy.

check new colour pairs against WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for focus rings and other non-text marks. Slate Ink on Chart Paper is 8.2:1. Sky Signal on Chart Paper is only 2.4:1, so it is never a focus ring on paper.
keep every transition inside the `prefers-reduced-motion` reset.
donts: add purple-to-blue gradients, glowing orbs, sparkle icons or other generic AI-startup styling.
make the site dark-only or use neon-on-black hacker styling. Light paper is the reference theme, and dark mode is a careful counterpart.
add shadows to cards, buttons or news rows.
use Survey Rule alone to carry meaning. It is a 1.4:1 hairline against Chart Paper, for structure only.
load fonts, scripts or images from other sites. The Content Security Policy blocks them.
